title: U.S. House · Georgia's 4th Congressional District
area: Parts of metro Atlanta east of the city, including DeKalb, Rockdale, and Newton counties.

context.text: Incumbent Hank Johnson (D), first elected in 2006, won the Democratic primary over Ansel Postell and Benedict Truman. James Duffie won the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Hank Johnson
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Ansel Postell and Benedict Truman.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 4th Congressional District (since 2007)

summary.text: Hank Johnson is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 4th Congressional District, first elected in 2006. A lawyer and former DeKalb County Commissioner, he is seeking re-election.

background.text: Born in Washington, D.C.; graduated from Clark College (now Clark Atlanta University) in 1976 and Texas Southern University's Thurgood Marshall School of Law in 1979.
Served as a DeKalb County Commissioner from 2000 to 2005, including as chair of the county's budget committee from 2002 to 2005; practiced law in Decatur, Georgia, for more than 25 years.

priorities.text: Says he will continue to advocate for a public health insurance option, push for greater consumer protections, and support increased investments in health care research.
Says he remains committed to advancing legislation that protects ecosystems, enhances EPA regulation, and promotes clean energy independence.
Says he remains committed to creating jobs, extending unemployment benefits when needed, protecting workers' rights, and supporting middle-class tax relief.

positions.summary: His official site says he has introduced, cosponsored, and voted for gun-violence-prevention bills including the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act, and supports legislation to establish universal background checks.
positions.quote: Congressman Johnson is a strong supporter of gun reform legislation. He has introduced, cosponsored, and voted for bills that work to end the epidemic of gun violence in America; including the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act. Congressman Johnson supports legislation that would establish universal background checks.

positions.summary: His official site says he will continue to advocate for a public health insurance option.
positions.quote: Looking ahead, he will continue to advocate for a public health insurance option, push for greater consumer protections, and support increased investments in health care research.

positions.summary: His official site says he has worked to protect tenants' rights as part of his housing agenda.
positions.quote: He has worked tirelessly to address the housing needs of Georgia's 4th District by advocating for increased funding for affordable housing programs, protecting tenants' rights, and supporting policies that combat housing discrimination.

positions.summary: His official site says he acknowledges the urgent need to combat climate change and remains committed to legislation promoting clean energy independence.
positions.quote: He acknowledges the urgent need to combat climate change, protect clean water, and curb harmful industrial practices.

positions.summary: His official site says he led efforts to increase wages by voting for the Raise the Wage Act.
positions.quote: Hank led efforts to increase wages by voting for the Raise the Wage Act and co-sponsored critical job-supporting bills like the Summer Jobs Act and the Federal Jobs Guarantee Development Act.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Judiciary (Courts, Intellectual Property, Artificial Intelligence, and the Internet Subcommittee; Oversight Subcommittee; The Administrative State, Regulatory Reform, and Antitrust Subcommittee) and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure (Aviation; Highways and Transit; Railroads, Pipelines, and Hazardous Materials subcommittees) in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Introduced the Cure Hepatitis C Act of 2026 with Rep. Diana DeGette and Rep. Mariannette Miller-Meeks, a bipartisan bill to create a nationwide, federally coordinated hepatitis C testing and treatment elimination program.

candidates.name: James Duffie
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: James Duffie is a U.S. Navy veteran and retired business executive, and the Republican nominee for Georgia's 4th Congressional District, campaigning for replacing the federal income tax with the FairTax and for stricter border enforcement.

background.text: Served in the U.S. Navy from 1961 to 1968; graduated from Avondale High School and attended the Georgia Institute of Technology; worked as a company president and CEO.

priorities.text: Says he will fight to eliminate the federal income tax and replace it with the FairTax, and to eliminate the IRS.
Says he will fight to keep borders secure and closed to unauthorized immigration.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to protect jobs by keeping the border secure, and that immigrants should assimilate.
Says Second Amendment rights should be protected.
